_comment: SPARK — S164 P5 (W1-C): atlas specs for the six CASTLE-SPAWN race units, one entry per unit,
consumed by scripts/build-sprite-atlas.mjs.
RETAINED IN-TREE, like every spec in this folder: S151 shipped three atlases and kept no spec, so
they could not be rebuilt or retuned — which is why a later 'redo the stink tower' needed a full
regeneration rather than a tweak.
⭐ ticksPerFrame MATCHES THE SHIPPED GOBLIN ROSTER — idle 7, walk 4, attack 5 — so a race unit
animates at the same cadence as every other creature on the board. These six are stat-identical
to each other by R94/R117, and matching the roster's cadence is the render-side half of reading
as peers rather than as a separate game.
⚠ `die` IS A FOURTH ROW AND NOTHING PLAYS IT YET. goblinRenderer maps three FSM states
(ATTACKING->attack, SEEKING->walk, else idle) and creatures are REMOVED the moment they are
killed, so there is no window in which a death row is visible. The builder is generic over the
states dict, so the row costs nothing to bake — it ships ready and the sim-side dying window is
its own piece of work. ticksPerFrame 5: a death should read deliberately, not snap past.
⚠ cellW/cellH are a FLOOR, not a cap — the builder widens the cell to fit whatever the subject
needs at full character height. The naga's tail and the orc's cleaver will push theirs wider, the
way the archer's shipped cell came out 234 rather than 200 because of his bow.

⛔ S164 OWNER REJECT 2 — enclosedWhiteLimitPct 0.003 -> 0.00004 ON EVERY UNIT. The owner looked at the built sheets: "the vampire is not cut out too well ... look the spaces between the wings, and some other areas - there is white background", and "the orc has a few like that". A census over all six atlases confirmed it and showed it was WIDER than the two he spotted — ~21,500 opaque near-white pixels total, with nagas (8,272) and demons (4,181) worse than vampires (2,591). This is the exact defect the matte's own docblock records for the bat rider one size-band up: enclosed white BELOW the limit is deliberately KEPT so eyes and blade glints survive, so pockets under the threshold ship as opaque blobs. MEASURED on the raw 1280x720 clip frames: the old 0.003 limit is 2,765 px, while the actual leaked pockets are 43..320 px (orcs) and 44..1,302 px (nagas) — every one of them far below it, which is why every unit leaked. 0.00004 puts the limit at ~37 px. ⚠ A SIZE THRESHOLD IS THE ONLY LEVER THAT WORKS HERE, and that was checked rather than assumed: brightness does NOT separate them (leaks measure 216..234 mean-min-channel, real features 220..244) because the leaks are ANTI-ALIASED background where white meets the ink outline, not pure white. Verified by eye on the rebuilt vampire sheet: wing gaps clean, eyes and teeth intact.

⛔ S164 OWNER REJECT 3 — THE ORC NEEDS ITS OWN LIMIT, because for THAT character eyes and leaks are the same size and cannot be separated by a size rule at all. Owner: "you have removed the white from the orcs eyes". Measured tradeoff on unit-orcs (leak px / head-band light px, the eye+tusk proxy): 0.00004 -> 42/377 · 0.0001 -> 210/614 · 0.0003 -> 696/1246 · 0.0008 -> 1233/1528 · 0.003 (original) -> 2253/2267. They move together, monotonically — there is no knee. 0.0003 is taken as the balance: ~69% of the leak gone, ~55% of the eye detail kept. ⚠ THE REAL FIX IS AT GENERATION, NOT IN THE MATTE, and it is filed rather than bodged: the design prompts must stop producing white pockets the size of an eye, and — separately — must stop baking a ground shadow at all (see the shadow note below).

⛔ S164 — THE BAKED GROUND SHADOW IS WRONG AND MUST COME OUT OF THE DESIGN PROMPTS. Owner: "the third vampire has a gray shadow while the rest have dark shadow - remember the shadow is of the players race color". He is right and the code agrees: goblinRenderer already draws a ring in the OWNER'S TINT at the creature's real position, and its docblock records that a BLACK shadow there was a measured no-op because the board background is pure black. So the game supplies the shadow, in the seat colour — the art must not. `sharedStyle` in design-spec.json currently ASKS for "a small soft dark oval shadow on the ground directly beneath the character"; that instruction is mine and it is the defect. Removing it also removes a whole class of matte ambiguity, because a mid-grey ellipse is neither near-white nor near-black and no rule catches it — which is exactly why one vampire frame kept a grey oval. ✅ DONE IN S165: the instruction was removed from BOTH sites (this spec's sharedStyle AND the script default every future spec inherits), and all 6 designs + 24 clips + 6 atlases were regenerated without it.

specs.name: unit-nagas
specs._why_sampleWindow: S165 — PER-STATE, AND THE S164 VALUE WAS RIGHT FOR ONE STATE AND WRONG FOR THE OTHER THREE. S164 answered the owner's "naga not coherent ... it looks twice bigger in different states" by putting sampleWindow 16 on ALL FOUR states. 16 frames is ~0.67s of a 4s clip, so attack and die were sampled entirely BEFORE the action happened: measured motion score (mean abs alpha delta between sampled frames) was 0.07 for idle and near-nothing for attack — the rows were frozen stills. The builder's own docblock says this knob is PER-STATE for exactly this reason: "a slow idle can take the whole clip while a drifting attack takes the front". MEASURED SWEEP, rebuilding each time: widening idle/attack/die 16 -> 48 left the union bbox EXACTLY unchanged at 295x200 and woke the rows up (idle 0.07 -> 15.90, attack -> 19.24, die -> 13.48), with subject-height spread of only 10px on idle and 13px on die. Widening WALK is the one that costs: 24/48/96 all inflate the cell 295 -> 336 while the height spread stays flat at 46-48px, so a wider walk window buys no coherence and pads every cell with dead space, which renders the naga SMALLER against its siblings. => walk stays at 16 (S164's finding, confirmed); idle, attack and die go to 48.

specs.name: unit-orcs
_why_orc_limit: ⭐ S165 — THE ORC KEEPS 0.0003, BUT NOT FOR THE REASON S164 GAVE. RE-MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.
S164 set this as an explicit COMPROMISE: for that character eyes and background leaks measured
the SAME SIZE with a monotonic curve and no knee, so 0.0003 kept ~55% of the eye detail and left
~31% of the leak. It filed the real fix as upstream — stop drawing white eyes.
⭐ THAT UPSTREAM FIX LANDED, AND IT WORKED. The S165 colour-cast clause gives this orc AMBER-GOLD
eyes and BONE-YELLOW tusks, so they are no longer near-white and the matte cannot see them. The
⛔ SO WHY NOT TIGHTEN TO 4e-05 LIKE ITS SIBLINGS? Because a rebuild at 4e-05 was measured and
compared frame by frame, and what it removes is no longer eyes — it is the CLEAVER'S STEEL
HIGHLIGHT. 545 px less leak, 2,607 px of character lost, and the loss lands on the blade edge,
⭐ AND THE LEAK IT LEAVES IS NOT WORTH THAT. At 0.0003 the largest surviving near-white pocket on
the whole sheet is 10 px — far below the 60 px the atlas guard treats as a visible patch, and
invisible at the 200 px cell. Tightening would trade an invisible defect for a visible one.
⚠ Re-test this if the orc is ever redesigned with a duller blade. The value is empirical, and
the measurement is the thing to repeat, not the number to inherit.

_outdir_convention: ⛔ public/art/race-units/, NOT public/godly/ — corrected in S165.
S164 wrote these six atlases to public/godly/unit-*/anim/. render/castleFrames.ts:83-87 states the
rule explicitly and it was already load-bearing when those were written: "Every existing atlas sits
under /godly/ because every existing atlas IS a godly combo's art. A castle is not a godly — it is
the board furniture every seat has from tick zero — and filing it under /godly/ would make the one
directory that currently means 'a combo shipped this' stop meaning that."
A castle-SPAWNED race unit is the same category as the castle: board furniture every seat has, not
a combo output. Moved while nothing in src/ referenced it yet, which is the cheap moment.
⚠ The builder writes <outDir>/<name>-atlas.png and <outDir>/<name>-anim.json, so the per-unit
'/anim/' subdirectory S164 used was never required by the tool — it was copied from the goblin
layout, where it IS required because each goblin owns a directory.
_veo_model_note: ⭐ THE THREE veo VARIANTS HAVE SEPARATE QUOTA POOLS, AND THAT IS WHAT UNBLOCKED THIS FOLDER.
Measured S165: veo-3.1-generate-preview answered 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED while veo-3.1-fast and
veo-3.1-lite BOTH accepted the same request, on the same key, in the same second. So the blocker
was never the account and never the billing - image generation on that same key worked throughout,
which is the tell: an account-wide problem would have stopped images too.
22 of the 24 clips are veo-3.1 (full). Two are veo-3.1-FAST: unit-vampires/attack and
unit-demons/die. Compared side by side at the REAL 200px cell size the two tiers are
indistinguishable - same linework, same colour, same character consistency - which is unsurprising
once you notice the pipeline throws away almost everything the bigger model buys: a 1280x720 clip
is sampled to 12 frames and matted into a 200px cell.
⚠ That finding is scoped to THIS pipeline at THIS output size. It is not a general licence to
drop tiers; gen-character-clips.mjs still defaults to the strongest model and only VEO_MODEL
⭐ AND THE VAMPIRE ATTACK IS FINALLY WEAPONLESS, ON THE FOURTH ATTEMPT. veo drifted a blade into
that clip on three generations across two sessions, under a bare negative, a stronger negative, and
an explicit positive ('both hands empty and visible in every frame'). None of them worked, because
none of them changed what the hands were DOING - and a hand at the salient point of a fast cartoon
action reads as a hand holding something. The fix was to change the VERB: the attack is now a BITE,
the jaws are the weapon, and the arms are explicitly parked back and down at his sides. First try.
_normalise_note: ⭐ normaliseStateScale: TRUE on every unit here. Each state is a separate veo generation and veo
picks its own zoom each time, so the four clips of one character disagreed about how big it is —
measured at FRAME 0, which is the same seed pose in all four rows and should therefore match:
hound walk 2.13x its own idle, hound die 1.98x, scarab walk 1.91x, souleater die 2.08x.
The owner caught it by eye before any measurement did: "size difference between row one and two
not consistent in hounds and lifestealers". The naga earned the same reject in S164.
⛔ PROMPTING ALONE DID NOT FIX IT. Anchoring the framing to the reference image in the SHARED clip
instruction repaired 3 of 5 rows and left the bat and the scarab at 1.77x and 1.91x, so the
remaining fix has to be deterministic rather than another dice roll.
The builder now measures frame 0 of each state, takes the median across states as the reference,
and rescales each state by ONE factor. Never per frame — a bat must still be allowed to spread
its wings during its own attack row.
